newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU fin ministers may have to decide Italy ERM move.
newsitem.headline: EU fin ministers may have to decide Italy ERM move.

text.p: Bringing the Italian lira back into the European Union's exchange rate mechanism (ERM) is so politically sensitive that EU finance ministers may have to be brought in to take the decision, EU officials say.

They said the monetary committee of central bank and finance ministry officials -- which took the decision to let in the Finnish markka in October -- may not have enough clout to agree a rate of entry for the lira.
Instead the committee could meet, then hand over the issue to the ministers to deal with.
"We won't spend too long at civil service level because this is so politically charged," said one EU official.

Italian Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said Thursday that Italy expected to return the lira to the ERM by the end of November, with 1,000-1,050 per mark seen as the best rate, while Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday there was no set date for the lira's re-entry into the ERM, but that Italy was likely to apply for re-entry this year.
But other countries, notably France, are wary of letting the lira back in at too low a rate. Paris wants a rate less than 1,000.
The first hurdle for Italy is to get enough agreement among its partners for a re-entry.
Officials say the monetary committee, which always meets on sensitive issues when financial markets are closed, could not possibly meet on the lira's re-entry and then not agree it.
Markets would have a field day against the currency when they re-opened.
It is widely assumed that the lira will re-join, but it is not a given. "Just because they want to do it does not mean it is going to happen," an official said.
In the unlikely event that there was too much opposition to the lira, officials said, the monetary committee chairman, Sir Nigel Wicks, would warn the Italians beforehand.
This means that once a committee meeting is convened it is next to certain that the lira will be brought in. The question will be the rate.
It is at that point, officials say, when the committee may decide it has to turn to their superiors. - Brussls newsroom: +32 2 287-6830
